headline: US BACKS GLOBAL ATOMIC'S NIGER URANIUM MINE WITH $414M DFC LOAN — FIRST AMERICAN INVESTMENT SINCE 2023 COUP
snippet: The US International Development Finance Corporation approved up to $414.2 million in debt financing for Global Atomic's Dasa uranium project in Niger on September 16-17, 2026 — the first major US resource investment in the country since American troops withdrew following the 2023 military coup; commercial production at Dasa is scheduled for the second half of 2028, pending conditions including a viable uranium export route, extensions to the mining agreement, and loan-repayment assurances. Niger is the world's seventh-largest uranium producer and the deal signals Washington rebuilding supply relationships it ceded to Russia and China after the coup.

headline: GOLD BREAKS $4,440 WEEKLY HIGH AS OIL SLIDES; SILVER SURGES 3% TO $67.18 ON COLLAPSING YIELDS
snippet: Spot gold extended its post-Fed rally to $4,439.80 on Friday September 18 — a new weekly high — as Brent crude retreated from $107 mid-week to $98.46 and US 10-year Treasury yields pulled back sharply, removing the inflation premium that had briefly capped precious metals after Wednesday's rate hike; silver followed with an even stronger 3.03% move, climbing from $65.21 to $67.18 intraday — the metal is now up 59% over twelve months despite a 46% correction from its January 2026 all-time high — with FXStreet technical analysts flagging $68.00 as the next resistance zone heading into the weekend.

headline: AYA GOLD & SILVER DRILLS 3,501 G/T Ag OVER 3.5M AT DEPTH AND 783 G/T Ag OVER 13M NEAR PIT AT MOROCCO'S ZGOUNDER
snippet: Aya Gold & Silver (TSX: AYA) released high-grade exploration results from its Zgounder Silver Mine in Morocco on September 16 — standout intercepts include 3,501 g/t Ag over 3.5 metres in the central at-depth zone and 783 g/t Ag over 13.0 metres near the existing open pit — as part of a 97-hole program spanning underground diamond, RC and percussion drilling aimed at mine-life extension; the company is simultaneously advancing a new exploration drift at the 1,825-metre level to open a fresh structural corridor, with high-grade silver mineralization confirmed open across both the central zone and pit periphery.

headline: URANIUM TERM PRICE BREAKS 2007 NOMINAL RECORD AT $96.50/LB — US UTILITIES LEAVE 52% OF DECADE NEEDS UNCOVERED
snippet: The uranium long-term contract price closed August 2026 at $96.50 per pound, surpassing the previous nominal all-time high of $95/lb set in 2007, as US utilities hold contracted deliveries of 174 million pounds against maximum requirements of 360 million pounds for 2026-2035 — leaving 186 million pounds, roughly 52% of anticipated needs, entirely uncovered over the next decade; the term-to-spot spread now exceeds $11/lb, and analysts at Bank of America cite the procurement gap — not new reactor demand — as the structural driver behind a $130/lb price target, with Cameco and Kazatomprom production cuts deepening the deficit.

headline: NdPr RARE EARTH COMPLEX DECLINES IN SYNC FOR FIRST TIME SINCE MAY — MAGNET METAL PRICES RETREAT ACROSS THE BOARD
snippet: The rare earth magnet complex fell together as a synchronized block in September 2026 for the first time since May — neodymium metal down 2.54%, praseodymium down 2.37% and the NdPr alloy benchmark (the primary permanent-magnet feedstock) retreating 1.98% — driven by sluggish downstream demand, pre-holiday ambiguity ahead of China's Mid-Autumn Festival, and transactions dominated by small rigid orders at low-priced cargo levels; the synchronized decline arrives as the November 10, 2026 expiry of China's expanded rare earth export-control pause approaches, adding a binary policy risk that is paralyzing mid-chain buyers from committing to restocking.

headline: GENERATION MINING LOCKS IN C$1.3B TO BUILD CANADA'S MARATHON COPPER-PALLADIUM MINE — Q4 CONSTRUCTION STARTS
snippet: Generation Mining (TSX: GENM) completed a C$1.3 billion construction financing package for the Marathon copper-palladium project in northwestern Ontario on September 14, 2026 — exceeding the $992 million construction estimate with $119 million of contingency — anchored by a C$200 million bought deal led by BMO Capital Markets (closing September 21), C$40 million from the Canada Growth Fund via private placement, and commitments from Wheaton Precious Metals and Glencore, which secured a concentrate offtake covering palladium, copper, platinum, gold and silver; early construction begins Q4 2026, making Marathon Canada's next primary palladium and copper producer.

headline: CHILE, ARGENTINA, BOLIVIA, PERU COORDINATE ON COPPER AND LITHIUM — FOUR NATIONS HOLD 40% OF GLOBAL LI RESERVES
snippet: A September 18 analysis of the South American joint declaration signed by Chile, Argentina, Bolivia and Peru on strategic minerals highlights the scale of the regional coordination: the four countries together hold roughly 40% of global lithium reserves and approximately 30% of global copper reserves, at a moment when the IEA projects copper supply could fall 25% short of demand by 2035; while no individual projects or production commitments were announced, the framework for geological data sharing, regulatory coordination and supply-chain integration could reshape how Western mining companies structure in-country partnerships across the region.

headline: TECK-ANGLO $54B MERGER ENTERS FINAL COUNTDOWN: SHAREHOLDERS MAILED TRANSMITTAL LETTERS FOR SHARE EXCHANGE
snippet: Teck Resources announced the mailing of a letter of transmittal to shareholders in connection with the planned merger of equals with Anglo American — the penultimate administrative step in the $54 billion deal that would create one of the world's largest diversified base-metals companies; as of early September, Chinese regulatory approval remained the sole outstanding condition with Anglo American communicating an expected closing window of September 2026 to March 2027, and the transmittal letter distribution suggests the timeline is compressing toward the earlier end of that range as shareholders prepare to exchange their Teck shares.

headline: SILVER: THE RATE HIKE IS PRICED IN, THE POSITIONING ISN'T — WHY RETAIL INVESTORS MAY BE SITTING OUT A STRUCTURAL MOVE
snippet: GoldSilver.com's September 2026 silver market analysis argues that the Federal Reserve's first rate hike since 2023 — the event precious metals investors had feared most — has now arrived and been absorbed with silver still above $67, confirming that the structural supply-deficit story is overriding the rate headwind; despite silver's 59% twelve-month gain, retail investor positioning in silver ETFs and futures remains well below historical peaks relative to the structural six-year deficit, suggesting the largest current holders are industrial users and institutional buyers rather than speculative longs who could create disorderly exits if sentiment turns.

headline: LITHIUM VS. COPPER: WHY ANALYSTS SAY THESE CRITICAL METALS DEMAND COMPLETELY DIFFERENT INVESTOR STRATEGIES
snippet: A September 2026 Discovery Alert analysis draws a sharp distinction between lithium and copper investment approaches for retail mining investors: lithium's volatile price cycle — up 81% year-on-year but already down 13% from its August 2026 peak — rewards shorter-horizon, catalyst-driven timing around production restarts and policy announcements, while copper's structural supply deficit (17-year average permitting timelines, flat primary mine supply growth despite surging data-centre and grid demand) suits longer-duration holding in established producers and royalty companies; the piece argues investors who treat both metals the same are likely to be wrong on both — exposed to lithium's whipsaws while underweight copper's structural squeeze.
